# Phase 2 automatic size integration

Opt in per request: set "auto_integrate": true, "reviewed": true on each candidate, and optionally "dry_run": true. Use one direct non-merge commit per candidate from the same base. Only existing firmware source files may change; Config.h is forbidden. Old requests (without auto_integrate) continue to measure only.

1. Existing eight-way independent measurement; reject invalid, failed, non-reducing candidates.
2. Rebuild the expected baseline, then try reducing candidates in descending Flash savings order, then descending RAM savings, then request order. Cherry-pick each onto last accepted commit, rebuild with the same portable toolchain, defer actual Git conflicts (never choose ours/theirs automatically) and restore the last accepted commit; reject and reset on build failure or failed size policy. Other Git apply errors stop the integration rather than silently rejecting a candidate. Both independent and cumulative decisions use the same policy: Flash and static RAM must both be non-increasing and at least one must decrease. Both deltas are recorded in JSON and Markdown. A RAM-only reduction is valid; trade-offs are rejected. Nine sign combinations are covered by the policy regression test.
3. Rebuild final firmware, verify sizes and Config.h, generate JSON/Markdown and ELF artifacts; prepare a Git bundle without write credentials.
4. A separate write job stages the measured commit; reusable normal CI checks the staged SHA and compares against the start SHA. Only after CI passes, a separate job publishes to experiment/size-reduction-phase2 with a branch lease. No PAT required; no master update. No publish in dry-run mode (a staging branch is retained for inspection).

Dry run may use historical ancestor base, without replacing current firmware. For real requests, the request commit and base must have identical Cart_Reader trees. Do not submit another request before the current run finishes; branch movement prevents publish. Hardware validation remains pending. The final report describes measurement decisions; the workflow's publish job establishes actual publication.

## Pending conflicts

Actual Git conflicts are recorded as pending_conflict, not rejected. The original base/head, conflicting paths, last accepted commit, final accepted firmware and measured baseline are recorded in integration.json and a separate *-pending.json file. Subsequent independent candidates still run. Once CI and publication finish, resolve pending candidates semantically against the current phase2 head, review them, and submit fresh one-commit candidates in a new auto request with the new calibrated baseline. Do not silently drop the other side of a conflict. In dry-run mode the queue is retained on the staging branch; it must not be applied to the real branch if the same changes are already present. The conflict helper is regression-tested with real Git conflicts, successful subsequent application, and a fatal non-conflict Git error.
